items.title: An untruncated linearity principle for Dedekind cuts forces the Cauchy and Dedekind reals to coincide

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 11.4.1 at source lines 1803-1813: if every Dedekind real merely carries an untruncated linearity function for the order, then the Cauchy and Dedekind reals coincide. The author's proof (source lines 1815-1839) is a construction rather than a citation: after recognising the assumption as an untruncated form of weak linearity (lines 1816-1817) and reducing to approximating Dedekind reals by Cauchy sequences of rationals (lines 1818-1819), it builds a nested sequence of rational intervals by repeated trisection in which the assumed function decides which subinterval still contains the cut (lines 1821-1832), and then verifies both the containment q_n < x < r_n and the geometric width estimate before concluding that the two endpoint sequences converge to x (lines 1834-1838). The statement is a one-line implication and hides the whole trisection construction.
